---
title: "What's new"
---

This course is an **early release**. Like an early-release book, it is complete enough to learn from, but it is still being finished: pages may change, and some parts are not available yet. Version numbers below 1.0 mark the early release. Version 1.0 follows when the course has been checked from start to finish.

Found a mistake or something unclear? Use "Report an issue" on any page, or [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml/issues).

## v0.5.1 · 12 November 2026

Each Self-study theme now prepares you for the DataLab iteration with the same number, and two new pages.

- **Themes regrouped.**
  - [Theme 1](self-study/theme-1.qmd) now ends with the [End-to-End ML Project](self-study/015_end_to_end_ml.ipynb).
  - [Theme 2](self-study/theme-2.qmd) is now Data Preparation & Understanding.
  - [Theme 3](self-study/theme-3.qmd) is now Modeling & Evaluation: it starts with the [Modeling & Evaluation](self-study/007_modeling_and_evaluation.ipynb) notebook, followed by linear regression, logistic regression and clustering.
- **New in Theme 2: [Leakage & Distribution Shift](self-study/12_leakage_and_distribution_shift.qmd).** With examples from real projects:
  - what a dataset represents;
  - data unlike the training data;
  - data from different sources;
  - leakage between training and test data;
  - how to make your development data match the data a model will be used on.

  It ends with review questions.
- **New in Iteration 2: [Understanding SMILES](datalab/iteration-2/00_understanding_smiles.qmd).** How to read a SMILES string, and what canonical SMILES are.
- **DataLab.**
  - The [project page](datalab/index.qmd) now starts with a short introduction to the problem.
  - Iterations 1 to 3 begin with what each iteration is for.
  - [Iteration 4](datalab/iteration-4/index.qmd) starts by rebuilding your models as pipelines.
  - [Iteration 6](datalab/iteration-6/index.qmd) suggests research papers to go further, and ends with writing up your solution as a portfolio project.
- The site has its own browser-tab icon and a preview image when you share a link.

## v0.5.0 · 12 November 2026

A new structure in six steps, and no textbook needed.

- **Six steps.** The [course route](start-here.qmd#the-course-route) has six steps. Each step is a Self-study theme followed by the DataLab iteration with the same number: Theme 1 and Iteration 1, Theme 2 and Iteration 2, and so on. At the end of each theme and each iteration, a note points you to what comes next.
- **No textbook needed.** The reading guides have been removed: the Self-study notebooks now teach everything the course needs. Many notebooks end with optional further reading, including a free online textbook.
  - New in Theme 2: [End-to-End ML Project](self-study/015_end_to_end_ml.ipynb), one small project with the Palmer penguins from start to finish, with a section for each stage of CRISP-DM.
  - New in Theme 3: [Linear Regression](self-study/012_linear_regression.ipynb), [Logistic Regression](self-study/013_logistic_regression.ipynb) and [Clustering](self-study/014_clustering.ipynb). Each notebook trains the model with scikit-learn first, then builds its algorithm by hand.
  - New sections: grid and random search in [Modeling & Evaluation](self-study/007_modeling_and_evaluation.ipynb), regression trees in [Decision Trees](self-study/009_decision_trees.ipynb), voting and extra-trees in [Random Forests](self-study/010_random_forests.ipynb), and AdaBoost and stacking in [Gradient Boosting](self-study/011_gradient_boosting.ipynb).
- **Overview pages for the Self-study.** [Self-study](self-study/index.qmd) and each of its six themes have an overview page that lists the activities in order, like the DataLab iterations.
- **The DataLab in six iterations**, one after each theme.
  - Iteration 2 ends with a new [Baseline](datalab/iteration-2/04_baseline.ipynb) notebook: your Iteration 1 models trained on your own dataset.
  - [Iteration 3](datalab/iteration-3/index.qmd) improves them with cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning, has a new clustering notebook, and ends with your first Kaggle submission. The classification and regression notebooks of the old Iteration 2 are now Iteration 3 notebooks 01 and 02; their old addresses forward to the new ones.
  - The old Iteration 3+ page is now three pages: [Iteration 4](datalab/iteration-4/index.qmd) (new data), [Iteration 5](datalab/iteration-5/index.qmd) (better models) and [Iteration 6](datalab/iteration-6/index.qmd) (your final solution).
- [Getting Started](self-study/001_getting_started.ipynb) introduces the penguins dataset, with photos of the three species and of the measurements.

## v0.4.1 · 4 November 2026

A new first page, and one textbook reading less.

- [What is Machine Learning?](self-study/00_what_is_machine_learning.qmd) is now an interactive introduction in eight short sections: fitting a line, measuring the fit with a cost, two parameters, gradient descent, polynomial regression, generalization (training and test data, underfitting and overfitting), regression vs classification, and supervised vs unsupervised learning. It ends with three review questions.
- The Machine Learning Landscape reading guide (Chapter 1 of the textbook) has been removed: the new page covers what the course needs from that chapter. [Classification](self-study/002_classification.ipynb), [Unsupervised Learning](self-study/004_unsupervised_learning.ipynb) and [Modeling & Evaluation](self-study/007_modeling_and_evaluation.ipynb) now refer to the new page instead.
- [Getting Started](self-study/001_getting_started.ipynb) follows on from the new page and points to the setup guide and How to use this course.

## v0.4.0 · 3 November 2026

The Kaggle competitions are open.

- **[OPV Molecule Stability 2026 Q4](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/opv-molecule-stability-2026-q4)** and **[OPV Molecule Energy Levels 2026 Q4](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/opv-molecule-energy-levels-2026-q4)**, until 31 December 2026. A new edition with new test molecules opens every quarter; the training data stays the same. How to take part: [Iteration 3+](datalab/iteration-3/index.qmd#the-kaggle-competitions).
- The test molecules are no longer in the course repository: download the sample submissions from the competition's Data tab (every edition has its own) into `data/003_kaggle_competition_data/`, which Git now ignores. A `git pull` removes the old files there.
- The public leaderboard scores half of the test molecules (100 of the 200), not 20%: a more reliable public score.
- When to submit and what to expect: Iterations 1, 2 and 3+ now say when your models are ready for Kaggle, and why the first score is usually lower than your cross-validation score.
- The data is described more precisely: the HOPV molecules were made and tested in solar cells; the lab and test molecules are candidates from a computational screening ([data/README.md](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml/blob/main/data/README.md)).

## v0.3.1 · 1 November 2026

Three corrections after a second review.

- [Random Forests](self-study/010_random_forests.ipynb): scikit-learn's `RandomForestClassifier` averages the trees' class probabilities instead of counting their votes; the notebook now explains the difference with the hand-made forest.
- [Modeling & Evaluation](self-study/007_modeling_and_evaluation.ipynb): more trees do not make a random forest overfit (they make it slower and the gains level off); the depth of the trees is what matters.
- [Iteration 3+](datalab/iteration-3/index.qmd): the experiment-log example now validates on lab molecules, which resemble the Kaggle molecules.

## v0.3.0 · 1 November 2026

Fixes and improvements after the first reviews of the course from a learner's point of view.

- **Evaluation matches the competitions.** Iteration 2 classification now uses stratified cross-validation and reports macro-F1 next to accuracy, with a majority-class baseline and new expected results. Modeling & Evaluation explains stratified folds and how macro and weighted F1 differ. Business Understanding says how success is measured.
- **Missing targets.** Iterations 1 and 2 remove only the rows where the target you predict is missing, which keeps far more molecules (72 instead of 46 in the starter dataset). A new exercise shows how much a score on a tiny test set depends on the split.
- **Iteration 1 clustering** explains the noise label `-1` and has a new exercise: find out why one descriptor decides the clusters, then scale the features.
- **Data leakage warning** in Iteration 2: the extra HOPV columns (gaps, efficiency, voltage, current, fill factor) are measurements, not features.
- **The data is described more precisely:** the molecules are real, the target values are generated for this course. Iteration 3+ is clearer about missing descriptor values in the lab and Kaggle molecules, how the competitions are scored, and how to keep an experiment log.
- **Finding your files:** the Iteration 2 notebooks say at the top which files they need and create; the setup guide has a notebook check and help for missing files. Files you create are now ignored by Git.
- **Self-study notebooks 005–011 show their output on the website**, including the decision trees and pipeline diagrams. Corrections in 005, 007, 008 (reproducible Optuna search), 009 and 010.
- pandas 3 wording (`str` instead of `object`), realistic disk space (about 3 GB), reading guides without page numbers of a specific print, open-access links, and smaller fixes.
- The DataLab iterations are now nested under DataLab in the menu. On released versions, the Colab button opens the notebook of that version.

## v0.1.0 · 1 November 2026

First public early release, adapted from the 2026/27 edition of the course at Breda University of Applied Sciences.

- **Self-study:** six themes with eleven notebooks and twelve reading and activity pages.
- **DataLab:** Iterations 1, 2 and 3+, with the course's own edition of the data, including a lab database for Iteration 3+.
- **Setup:** one Python environment (Python 3.13, managed with uv) with every package the course uses.
- **License:** content [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), code MIT, so you can reuse the course in your own teaching.
